dataset.name: NIH ChestX-ray14
dataset.images: row_id + .png; licensed local image root supplied by operator
dataset.prior_study_patient_overlap: allowed and disclosed; shared-panel model replication, not fresh-patient confirmation
dataset.additional_manifests: CheXpert and COCO ordered manifests must be constructed once using README section 4 and shared before model runs

primary.locus: consumed final visual feature block, before connector
primary.score: max present-candidate logit minus max absent-candidate logit
primary.primary_family: 22 models x 3 datasets x 6 questions x 5 clinical/object contrasts = 1980; separate bootstrap within dataset, shared across models
primary.simultaneous_interval: two-sided max-absolute-centered-Z with fixed per-contrast bootstrap SD

probe.refit: bootstrap training patients with replacement seeds1,2, retain all rows per sampled patient multiplicity; refit train scaler and all6logistic probes with fixed projection; COCO resample images

intervention.random_rng: PCG64; one 119xD standard_normal draw then row normalization; saved vectors authoritative
intervention.sham: after random draw, permute each clinical normal in concept order; save all permutations
intervention.tensor_policy: preserve special tokens and padding; perturb consumed image tokens; record branch selection

templates.IY: Is there {finding} in {image_phrase}? Answer yes or no.
templates.WY: Does {image_phrase} show {finding}? Answer yes or no.
templates.IA: Is there {finding} in {image_phrase}? Answer A if the finding is present and B if it is absent. Reply with A or B only.
templates.IB: Is there {finding} in {image_phrase}? Answer B if the finding is present and A if it is absent. Reply with A or B only.
templates.WA: Does {image_phrase} show {finding}? Answer A if the finding is present and B if it is absent. Reply with A or B only.
templates.WB: Does {image_phrase} show {finding}? Answer B if the finding is present and A if it is absent. Reply with A or B only.

FGOBJ.questions: six FINE-GRAINED COCO object concepts (handbag, book, backpack, traffic light, knife, cell phone), not the six protocol COCO concepts
FGOBJ.labels: presence from the 2017 instance annotations of the row's own split, crowd instances count as present (the rule of manifests.build_coco); APPENDED to the frozen COCO labels.csv without changing one existing row, cohort.csv and the roles untouched, provenance in manifests/fgobj.json (python -m cftransfer.fgobj --build-labels)
FGOBJ.selection: prespecified, outcome-free: >= 10 positives among the 400 calibration rows and among the 600 test rows, >= 567 training positives (bicycle's, the weakest easy concept), mean relative instance area below the median of the six easy concepts (0.02252); then calibration positives descending, ties by mean area ascending, then category id
FGOBJ.directions: own clean baseline + 6 fine-grained directions (fgobj:<concept>) + the family's OWN 119 random directions (fgobjrand:###) + the question's own sham (fgobjsham:<concept>) = 127 conditions per question, byte for byte CORE's grid shape
FGOBJ.fit: the block's own seed-0 projection R and TRAIN-ONLY scaler (never refitted), LogisticRegression(C=1, lbfgs, 2000 iterations, random_state 0) on the SAME training rows, lifted with fit.direction_from_projected; the random family and shams are fit_locus's construction re-drawn from PCG64(3), so an FGOBJ cell is graded against a random p95 and a sham of its own
FGOBJ.prep: python -m cftransfer.fgobj --model-key K --dataset coco  (CPU, seconds; writes fits/vis.last/fgobj_seed0.npz with the calibration-row probe and control logits the readability rule needs)
FGOBJ.added: 2026-09-16; addendum, enqueued explicitly (four shards, CORE's budget); a CONTROL for a handful of COCO blocks, not the whole grid
FGOBJ.rationale: the headline contrast is 29 of 246 chest cells owned against 101 of 120 COCO cells, and a reviewer can answer that COCO differs in DIFFICULTY rather than in concept type. The six easy COCO concepts give the natural-image side no hard cells, so the difficulty-matched chest-versus-COCO comparison is starved. FGOBJ makes the natural-image side span the chest side's difficulty range, with everything but the six categories held fixed.
FGOBJ.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what fgobj: the 6x6 write matrix, O_q with the percentile interval and the 6x5 max-T verdict, the family's own random p95 and sham, the readable and answer-capable grades from the calibration rows, and the block-level comparison against the block's own six easy-COCO CORE cells (ownership rate, median clean-answer AUROC, median probe selectivity per family). scripts/mayo/robustness_round2.py adds the pooled difficulty-matched comparison.

FGOBJ_CALIBRATION.questions: the same six fine-grained COCO concepts, clean
FGOBJ_CALIBRATION.baseline: own (the clean forward IS the measurement)
FGOBJ_CALIBRATION.added: 2026-09-16; addendum, enqueued explicitly (one shard), no prep of its own
FGOBJ_CALIBRATION.rationale: the matched comparison pools chest, easy-COCO and fine-grained-COCO cells on clean-answer AUROC. CALIBRATION measures that on the 400 calibration rows for the first two; this module measures it the same way, on the same rows, for the third, so no group is matched on a differently estimated number.
FGOBJ_CALIBRATION.analysis: folded into cftransfer.analysis --what fgobj; until it is scored the fine-grained cells carry no clean-answer AUROC and the matched comparison refuses to pool them

DOSE.cohort: first 200 test rows in cohorts.csv order

LOCUS.locus: connector_output (single consumed image embedding stream; family adaptation recorded)

ALTDIR.directions: 6dom+6pattern+6orth+6resid (24 steered conditions per question; no baseline rows)

direction_families.dom: difference of class means mu_pos - mu_neg in the projected, train-scaled 512-d space (known-label training rows)
direction_families.pattern: Haufe pattern Sigma w, Sigma = covariance of the projected, train-scaled features over all training rows, w = seed-0 logistic normal
direction_families.orth: seed-0 logistic normal with its component in the span of the other five concepts' logistic normals removed (512-d space); fraction of norm removed recorded
direction_families.resid: logistic normal (same C, iterations, seed 0) refitted on features residualised column-wise against the other concepts' binary labels (intercept + labels) on the training rows where the concept's label and every used covariate label are known; covariates are dropped one at a time, worst first, while one has fewer than 5 rows in a class on those rows or the rows fall below 25% of the concept's own known rows (CheXpert); a concept single-class on its usable rows keeps the logistic normal (fallback); resid_covariates_used / resid_rows_used / resid_fallback / resid_retention_fraction and the cosine to the original normal are recorded

ALTDIR.lift: every family is mapped to model space exactly as the logistic normal: v = normalize(P @ (u / max(s, 1e-8)))
ALTDIR.prep: python -m cftransfer.altdir --model-key K --dataset D  (CPU; writes fits/vis.last/altdir_seed0.npz)
ALTDIR.added: 2026-09-14; not part of the planned campaign total (see total_planned_outcomes.ALTDIR_rows_addendum); enqueued explicitly
ALTDIR.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what altdir: per family W (6x6), within-family O_q with 2,000-draw patient-bootstrap percentile interval and 6x5 max-T verdict, own write minus the strongest logistic competitor from CORE, per-concept cosines

EXTCOMP.directions: one logistic direction per extra dataset label (no baseline rows; CORE baseline reused)
EXTCOMP.support_rule: label kept when the training rows hold >= 100 known positives and >= 100 known negatives

chexpert.Pleural Other: 12 known negatives in the training rows (< 100)

EXTCOMP.fit: as the protocol normals: seed-0 projection P, train-only scaler, LogisticRegression(C=1, lbfgs, 2000 iterations, random_state 0) on the label's known-label training rows; lifted with normalize(P @ (w / max(s, 1e-8)))
EXTCOMP.prep: python -m cftransfer.extcomp --model-key K --dataset D  (CPU; writes fits/vis.last/extcomp_seed0.npz with cosines to the six normals and calibration/test AUROC)
EXTCOMP.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what extcomp: W_q,extra per extra direction, extended ownership O^ext_q = W_qq - max over the five protocol competitors and the extras with the 2,000-draw percentile interval, extras beating W_qq, verdict over the extended 6 x (5 + K) max-T family

TOKENW.directions: 6 logistic directions x 2 token-weighting variants = 12 steered conditions per question (no baseline rows; CORE baseline reused)

variants.tokenw: weight_t = T * softmax_t(score_t), score_t = the token's projected, train-scaled feature dotted with the concept's logistic normal (temperature 1); mean weight 1
variants.topq: the top 25% of consumed tokens by score_t (round(0.25 T), at least 1) get weight T/k (= 4), the rest 0; mean weight 1

TOKENW.write: h'_t = h_t + alpha * weight_t * ||h_t|| * v_c per consumed token (hooks.token_weights); same total dose as CORE's uniform write
TOKENW.added: 2026-09-14; addendum, enqueued explicitly; no prep beyond fits/vis.last/seed0.npz
TOKENW.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what tokenw: per variant W (6x6), O_q with percentile interval and 6x5 max-T verdict, own weighted write minus the strongest uniform logistic competitor of CORE

PRECISION.cohort: first 200 test rows in cohorts.csv order
PRECISION.directions: the CORE grid: baseline + 6 clinical + 119 random + question sham = 127 (own baseline per setting)

settings.fp32: model weights and forward in float32; CORE batch composition
settings.batch1: bf16 weights; batch size 1 for every condition, baseline included

PRECISION.runner: python -m cftransfer.runner ... --module PRECISION --numerics fp32|batch1; outcomes carry the setting in the `numerics` column (every other module: bf16-batched)
PRECISION.added: 2026-09-14; addendum, enqueued explicitly as two tasks (PRECISION-fp32, PRECISION-batch1)
PRECISION.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what precision: per setting W and O on the 200 rows against CORE on the same rows, max |dW| over the 6x6 clinical cells, dO per question, agreement of the two point verdicts (own > strongest competitor, own > random p95)

ANSDIR.directions: 6 answer directions a_d + the coordinate-permutation sham of a_q = 7 steered conditions per question (no baseline rows; CORE baseline and random family reused)
ANSDIR.prep: python -m cftransfer.ansdir --model-key K --dataset D --n-train 3000 (GPU, enqueued by enqueue --modules ANSDIR as the module's prep task): clean forwards of the six primary-template questions on the first 3,000 training-cohort rows in manifest order, fp32 answer margins to outcomes/ANSDIR_prep.parquet; per question a ridge regression of the margin on the projected, train-scaled 512-d features (seed-0 P and scaler; alpha by 5-fold CV over {0.1, 1, 10, 100}), lifted with normalize(P @ (w / max(s, 1e-8))) to a_q; fits/vis.last/ansdir_seed0.npz holds a_q, the CV R^2, cos(a_q, w_q) and the 6x6 cosine matrix to the logistic normals
ANSDIR.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what ansdir: W^a (6x6), O^a_q with the 2,000-draw percentile interval and 6x5 max-T verdict, steering reference against the CORE random p95 and the a-sham, own answer write minus the strongest logistic competitor of CORE, cosines / CV R^2

ALTDIRD.directions: 6 dom_disp + 6 pattern_disp = 12 steered conditions per question (no baseline rows; CORE baseline reused)
ALTDIRD.lift: a displacement u in the standardised 512-d space is lifted as its minimum-norm preimage x = R (R^T R)^{-1} diag(s) u (R = the seed-0 projection), unit-normalised; the coefficient lift R diag(1/s) beta of the logistic normals and of the ALTDIR families is unchanged
ALTDIRD.prep: python -m cftransfer.altdir --model-key K --dataset D  (CPU; appends dom_disp/pattern_disp vectors, the R^T R / D eigenvalue spectrum and the extended cosine matrices to fits/vis.last/altdir_seed0.npz without changing existing arrays)
ALTDIRD.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what altdird: per family W (6x6), within-family O_q with interval and 6x5 max-T verdict, own write minus the strongest logistic competitor of CORE, cosines to the logistic normal and to the coefficient-lifted dom / pattern

ATTR.questions: 3 attribute questions (view_AP, sex_F, age_60; protocol templates with the attribute phrase) + the 6 clinical questions

attribute_phrases.age_60: a patient aged sixty or older

ATTR.support_rule: >= 100 known training rows per class (both chest sets qualify on all three attributes)
ATTR.directions: 3 attribute directions (fitted like the protocol normals) + 6 clinical normals + the question's sham; attribute questions also score their clean baseline (11 conditions), clinical questions reuse CORE's baseline (10 conditions); no random family (CORE's random p95 is the reference for clinical questions; attribute questions are referenced against their sham only)
ATTR.prep: python -m cftransfer.attr --model-key K --dataset D  (CPU; writes fits/vis.last/attr_seed0.npz with directions, shams, cosines to the six normals, calibration-row probe and type->random-label control logits)
ATTR.baseline: attribute questions: own; clinical questions: reuse CORE
ATTR.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what attr: 9x9 write matrix (questions x directions), ownership of every question over the family {3 attributes + 6 clinical} with interval and max-T verdict, readability of the attribute probes (calibration rows, selectivity vs the 20 type->random-label controls) and answer AUROC of the clean attribute questions on the test rows

ANSDIRT.directions: baseline + 6 IY-fitted answer directions a_d + the a-sham of q = 8 conditions per (question, template); 40 per question over the five templates
ANSDIRT.prep: fits/vis.last/ansdir_seed0.npz from the ANSDIR prep (python -m cftransfer.ansdir; enqueue emits it)
ANSDIRT.added: 2026-09-15; addendum, enqueued explicitly; INELIGIBLE templates are dropped as in PROMPT
ANSDIRT.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what ansdirt: per template W^a (6x6), O^a_q with interval and 6x5 max-T verdict, the a-sham reference, the cross comparison against the logistic competitors and random p95 of PROMPT under the same template (its two designated concepts), and transfer counts of the IY-owned a_q cells (from --what ansdir) that stay owned under each template

VALID.directions: baseline+6clinical+119random+question_sham (the CORE grid with the block's seed-0 directions; no new fit)
VALID.rows: 200: one frontal per patient of the official CheXpert validation split (200 patients, 202 frontals), selected and ordered by the CheXpert Plus hash rules (manifests.build_chexpert_valid); labels are the radiologist consensus of CheXpert-v1.0 valid.csv (manifests/release.json `valid`, label_source radiologist), not the labeler output of the other roles
VALID.added: 2026-09-15; addendum, enqueued explicitly; images PNG/valid/* of the CheXpert Plus zips (scripts/mayo/extract_chexpert_valid.py); enqueue also emits a features task for the valid rows (features/valid/<locus>.npz) that the module task does not wait for
VALID.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what valid: the CORE grade on the valid rows (W_qq, strongest competitor, O_q with interval, 6x5 max-T verdict from 2,000 paired draws at n = 200, random p95 / |sham| reference on those rows), answer capability of the clean answers against the radiologist labels (campaign rule), probe readability on the valid features against the 20 control probes when extracted, and the paired comparison with the block's CORE grade on the 600 labeler-labelled test rows (per-concept readable / answer-capable / owned, O_q on both, counts of agreeing verdicts)

ATTRRAND.questions: the 3 attribute questions of ATTR only (view_AP, sex_F, age_60)
ATTRRAND.directions: the protocol's own 119 random directions (fits/vis.last/seed0.npz random_vectors, the PCG64(0) draw CORE scores); no new directions, no baseline rows, no prep of its own
ATTRRAND.rationale: ATTR referenced attribute cells against their sham alone while clinical cells had the 119-random p95, so the attribute-versus-finding ownership comparison used two different steering references; ATTRRAND gives an attribute cell the same random p95 bar as a clinical cell
ATTRRAND.baseline: reuse ATTR (the attribute questions' own clean baseline)
ATTRRAND.analysis: folded into cftransfer.analysis --what attr: each attribute cell gains random_p95 / random_n / rank_in_random_family from this module and records steering_reference_sham_only (the old rule), steering_reference_matched (W_qq > 0, > random p95, > |sham|) and steering_reference_rule, which names the reference the cell used; clinical cells are unchanged

ATTRQ.questions: the 3 attribute questions of ATTR only (view_AP, sex_F, age_60), each under 3 phrasings
ATTRQ.directions: none: clean forwards only (no writes, no reference family)
ATTRQ.rationale: cheap per-block eligibility pass for the ATTR / ATTRRAND control: how well the model answers each non-clinical attribute question under three phrasings, on the calibration rows, with no writes and no reference family. It exists because a cell whose clean answer no direction can move cannot be owned for reasons that have nothing to do with whether the concept is clinical, so pooling such cells makes the attribute-versus-finding comparison unfair in both directions.
ATTRQ.baseline: own (the clean forward IS the measurement)
ATTRQ.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what attrq: per attribute and phrasing the question text, n_pos / n_neg, clean-answer AUROC and Brier, the one-sided 95% lower bound, the answer-capable flag, and the selected phrasing with the reason; written to summary.json under `attrq`. analysis --what attr then reads the written phrasing's calibration-row numbers from it, so an attribute cell and a clinical cell carry answerability measured on the same rows.

VALIDFIT.cohort: test (the write); the FIT uses the 200 radiologist-labelled `valid` rows
VALIDFIT.directions: 6 expert-label directions (vfit:<concept>); no baseline rows, no random family and no sham of its own -- CORE's baseline, 119-random family and question sham are the references
VALIDFIT.fit: the six concept probes refitted on the known-label `valid` rows (role valid, label_source radiologist) with the protocol's own probe settings: the block's seed-0 projection R and its TRAIN-ONLY scaler mu/s (never refitted on 200 rows), LogisticRegression(C=1, lbfgs, 2000 iterations, random_state 0), lifted with normalize(R @ (w / max(s, 1e-8))); features from features/valid/<locus>.npz (the VALID feature task)
VALIDFIT.cross_fitting: 5 folds over PATIENTS (KFold shuffled, seed 0, over the sorted unit ids), so every valid row is scored by a direction not fitted on it
VALIDFIT.cpu_report: raw cosine (model space and projected 512-d) and covariance-whitened cosine (<a,b>_Sigma / sqrt(<a,a>_Sigma <b,b>_Sigma), Sigma = covariance of the projected, train-scaled TRAINING features) between each expert-label direction and the corresponding report-label direction; held-out probe AUROC against the expert labels and against the report-derived (labeler) labels of the same rows; the seed-0 report-label direction's AUROC on those rows for reference
VALIDFIT.prep: python -m cftransfer.validfit --model-key K --dataset chexpert  (CPU; writes fits/vis.last/validfit_seed0.npz)
VALIDFIT.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what validfit: W^e (6x6), O^e_q with the 2,000-draw percentile interval and the 6x5 max-T verdict, CORE's steering reference (W^e_qq > 0, > the 119-random p95, > |sham|), own expert write minus the strongest logistic competitor of CORE, and the prep's cosines / AUROCs per concept

PROJSEED.directions: per projection seed: 6 refit directions (proj:<concept>) + that projection's own 119 random directions (projrand:###) + the question's sham (projsham:<concept>) = 126 conditions per question and seed; no baseline rows
PROJSEED.fit: R_k = PCG64(k).standard_normal((D, 512)) / sqrt(512) (the protocol's projection construction with the seed replaced); the train-only scaler is recomputed in that projected space; the six probes are refitted on the SAME training rows and known-label masks with the same hyperparameters (C=1, lbfgs, 2000 iterations, random_state 0); the random family and shams are the same construction re-drawn from PCG64(k) in that projection
PROJSEED.fit_seed_column: the outcomes carry the PROJECTION seed (1 or 2) in the fit_seed column; direction ids are seed-independent
PROJSEED.prep: python -m cftransfer.projseed --model-key K --dataset D  (CPU; writes fits/vis.last/projseed_seed1.npz and projseed_seed2.npz with the model-space cosines to the seed-0 directions)
PROJSEED.added: 2026-09-16; addendum, enqueued explicitly, ONE SHARD PER PROJECTION SEED (runner --fit-seed); intended for a handful of representative blocks, not the whole grid
PROJSEED.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what projseed: per seed W^k (6x6), O^k_q with the 2,000-draw percentile interval and the 6x5 max-T verdict, that projection's OWN random p95 and sham as the steering reference, the model-space cosine to the seed-0 direction, and the count of verdicts / ownership decisions that agree with the block's CORE grade on the same rows

TOWERSWAP.cohort: first 200 test rows in cohorts.csv order
TOWERSWAP.directions: the CORE grid: baseline + 6 clinical + 119 random + question sham = 127 (own baseline), with the DIRECTIONS OF THE TOWER IN USE -- the donor block's seed-0 fit, reused unchanged
TOWERSWAP.model: the block's own reader (multimodal projector + language model) with the PARTNER checkpoint's vision tower loaded in its place; protocol.TOWERSWAP_PAIRS pairs gemma3-4 with medgemma-4 and gemma3-27 with medgemma-27
TOWERSWAP.swap_feasibility: verified from the staged checkpoints (python -m cftransfer.towerswap): gemma-3-4b-it and medgemma-4b-it have IDENTICAL tensor name sets (883 each) and identical shapes for vision_tower (437 tensors, 416.9M params), multi_modal_projector (2) and language_model (444), with 0/437 tower tensors bitwise identical (MedSigLIP vs SigLIP); the same holds for gemma-3-27b-it vs medgemma-27b-it (1247 tensors). gemma-3-12b-it vs medgemma-27b-it fails as expected: mm_input_projection_weight (1152,3840) vs (1152,5376) and 48 vs 62 language-model layers.
TOWERSWAP.verification: every replaced tensor is torch.equal to the donor checkpoint's tensor after the runtime dtype cast, and every parameter and buffer outside the tower keeps its (dtype, shape, sum, sum|x|, NaN count) signature; the receipt is written to outcomes/TOWERSWAP/swap-<shard>.json
TOWERSWAP.four_combinations: the two crossed arms are this module on the two blocks of a pair; the two native arms are those blocks' own CORE grade restricted to the same 200 rows (analysis.core row_limit), so no GPU time is spent re-running CORE
TOWERSWAP.added: 2026-09-16; addendum, enqueued explicitly, only for the models in TOWERSWAP_PAIRS
TOWERSWAP.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what towerswap: per combination (tower, reader) the 6x6 write matrix, W_qq, O_q with the 2,000-draw percentile interval, the 119-random p95 / |sham| steering reference and the 6x5 max-T verdict; within the block the paired crossed-minus-native contrasts; and, when the partner block is packaged, the reader effect at fixed tower and the tower effect at fixed reader over the six questions

REPLAY.cohort: first 200 test rows in cohorts.csv order
REPLAY.directions: the CORE grid (127 configurations, own baseline) with the SOURCE block's seed-0 directions, random family and sham -- identical for every reader of the shared-tower group
REPLAY.mechanism: the consumed block's output is overwritten with the source block's stored tensor before the steering hook reads it (cftransfer.replay.ReplayHook registers on the same module with prepend=True after LocusHook, so it runs first and LocusHook computes the token norms and the write on the replayed tensor); the outcome schema is unchanged
REPLAY.shared_tower_groups: verified bitwise identical in the staged checkpoints: SigLIP 437/437 tensors across gemma3-4 / gemma3-12 / gemma3-27, MedSigLIP 437/437 across medgemma-4 / medgemma-27, CLIP ViT-L/14-336 391/391 across llava15-7 / llava15-13; SigLIP vs MedSigLIP 0/437. llavamed-7 joins the CLIP group: the same 391 tensors in the same shapes under the vision_tower.vision_model.* spelling, equal up to the fp16 -> bf16 storage change (max |difference| 0.047, 0 exactly equal after the cast), which is precisely the difference replaying one stored tensor into both readers removes; it is the grid's only shared-tower pair whose readers are a general and a medical model.
REPLAY.prep: python -m cftransfer.replay --model-key SOURCE --dataset D (GPU; one tower pass over the 200 rows, writes runs/SOURCE/D/replay/vis.last.npz with the ORIGINAL bits of the captured tensor)
REPLAY.note: the tower still runs during the module, so a replay block costs what the same CORE grid costs on the same rows; what it buys is an exactly identical input, not speed
REPLAY.added: 2026-09-16; addendum, enqueued explicitly, only for the models in REPLAY_SOURCE
REPLAY.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what replay: the CORE grade on the replayed tensors (core() on the REPLAY parquet), the paired comparison against the block's own CORE grade on the same rows, the recorded drift between this reader's own tower output and the stored tensor, and, when the group's other blocks are packaged, the cross-reader comparison on byte-identical inputs

SEMEND.directions: baseline + 6 label directions concept:<c> + 6 answer directions ans:<c> + the question's label sham sham:<q> + the question's answer sham anssham:<q> + 18 random directions = 33 conditions per (question, endpoint). Both families therefore have a FULL 6x6 write matrix on every endpoint, so the campaign's ownership rule applies unchanged AND the spillover of one direction onto the other five concepts' endpoints is measured.
SEMEND.endpoints: see the top-level `semend` block: NY negated question (sign -1), DA/DB counterbalanced two-finding forced choice, RF finding-word log-probability in a report continuation
SEMEND.reference: each endpoint gets its own clean baseline and its own steering reference: the own signed effect must be positive, above all 18 random directions (rank 1 of 19) and above that family's own |sham|. Ownership is the campaign rule: the steering reference plus positive max-T lower bounds over the five-competitor family.
SEMEND.prep: python -m cftransfer.semend --model-key K --dataset D (CPU; freezes the strongest competitor per question from the block's CORE write matrix and the exact rendered prompt of every (question, endpoint) into fits/vis.last/semend_seed0.npz). It requires fits/vis.last/ansdir_seed0.npz, so SEMEND is enqueued with or after ANSDIR.
SEMEND.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what semend: per endpoint and per family the 6x6 write matrix, W_qq, O_q with the 2,000-draw percentile interval, the 18-random / sham steering reference and the 6x5 max-T verdict; the affirmative-versus-negated signed change and its across-question correlation with CORE; the counterbalanced forced-choice probability and the order bias; the report-continuation delta log p of the finding word; and the incremental-validity regression described above
SEMEND.incremental_validity: the analysis asks whether OWNERSHIP predicts behaviour on these endpoints beyond what is already known. Per cell (question, endpoint, family) it records the intended change on the question's own endpoint, the unintended change of the same direction on the other five concepts' endpoints, and their difference (the selectivity of the change). Pooled over cells it regresses that difference on (i) the CORE write magnitude W_qq, (ii) the probe selectivity S, (iii) the clean-answer AUROC, and then adds (iv) the CORE ownership indicator and O_q, reporting the added coefficients, their patient-bootstrap intervals and the change in explained variance, separately for the label and the answer direction. Cells that meet the steering reference but are NOT owned are kept as their own group and compared with the owned cells directly, since that contrast is what ownership would have to explain.

TOWERSWAPD.directions: the block's own seed-0 fit, unchanged

TOWERSWAPD.swap_feasibility: verified from the staged checkpoints (python -m cftransfer.towerswap): gemma-3-4b-it and medgemma-4b-it have IDENTICAL tensor name sets (883 each) and identical shapes for vision_tower (437 tensors, 416.9M params), multi_modal_projector (2) and language_model (444), with 0/437 tower tensors bitwise identical (MedSigLIP vs SigLIP); the same holds for gemma-3-27b-it vs medgemma-27b-it (1247 tensors). gemma-3-12b-it vs medgemma-27b-it fails as expected: mm_input_projection_weight (1152,3840) vs (1152,5376) and 48 vs 62 language-model layers.
TOWERSWAPD.verification: every replaced tensor is torch.equal to the donor checkpoint's tensor after the runtime dtype cast, and every parameter and buffer outside the tower keeps its (dtype, shape, sum, sum|x|, NaN count) signature; the receipt is written to outcomes/TOWERSWAPD/swap-<shard>.json
TOWERSWAPD.four_combinations: the two crossed arms are this module on the two blocks of a pair; the two native arms are those blocks' own CORE grade restricted to the same 200 rows (analysis.core row_limit), so no GPU time is spent re-running CORE
TOWERSWAPD.added: 2026-09-17; addendum, enqueued explicitly, only for the models in TOWERSWAP_PAIRS
TOWERSWAPD.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what towerswap: per combination (tower, reader) the 6x6 write matrix, W_qq, O_q with the 2,000-draw percentile interval, the 119-random p95 / |sham| steering reference and the 6x5 max-T verdict; within the block the paired crossed-minus-native contrasts; and, when the partner block is packaged, the reader effect at fixed tower and the tower effect at fixed reader over the six questions
TOWERSWAPD.purpose: the same crossed arm as TOWERSWAP with the block's OWN directions instead of the donor tower's, so the pair separates the two factors a tower swap changes at once: TOWERSWAPD against TOWERSWAP isolates the direction the tower was fitted on, and TOWERSWAPD against the native arm isolates the representation itself

addenda_notes.PROJSEED: 907,200 rows per block (453,600 per projection seed). The addenda table states the whole-grid figure by its own convention (per model over all datasets x 22 models); the module is intended for a handful of representative blocks, not the whole grid.
addenda_notes.ATTRRAND: 214,200 rows per chest block (NIH + CheXpert x 22 models)
addenda_notes.TOWERSWAP: 152,400 rows per crossed arm; the table follows the campaign convention (all datasets x 22 models), but the module is defined only for the four models of TOWERSWAP_PAIRS and is budgeted for the gemma3-4 / medgemma-4 pair on NIH and CheXpert (4 arms, ~10.9 GPU-h measured from those blocks' own CORE throughput), COCO optional (+5.3 GPU-h). The two native arms cost nothing: they are CORE restricted to the same 200 rows.
addenda_notes.REPLAY: 152,400 rows per block; the table follows the campaign convention, but the module is defined only for the seven blocks of the three shared-tower groups (REPLAY_SOURCE). One dataset per group costs ~5.7 GPU-h (LLaVA-1.5 pair), ~7.5 (MedGemma pair) and ~11.2 (Gemma 3 triple), plus a tower-only tensor prep of well under 0.1 GPU-h per source block.
addenda_notes.SEMEND: 475,200 rows per block; budgeted for at most 8 blocks, staged behind a 3-block stop rule. The GPU cost is set by the number of forwards, not the number of outcomes: 32 steered conditions are one batch-32 forward, so the full 33-condition grid costs exactly what a 25-condition grid would (7.3-19.5 GPU-h per block on the measured throughput of those blocks' own CORE runs).
addenda_notes.ATTRQ: 3,600 rows per chest block (3 attributes x 3 phrasings x 400 calibration rows); the table follows the campaign convention (NIH + CheXpert x 22 models)
addenda_notes.FGOBJ: 457,200 rows per COCO block, byte for byte CORE's grid shape on six new questions; the table follows the campaign convention (COCO x 22 models), but the module is a CONTROL and is budgeted for a handful of COCO blocks chosen for family coverage, not for the whole grid. Measured cost per block is that block's own CORE cost (same 6 x 127 x 600 grid): 3.2-16.4 GPU-h over the 17 COCO blocks whose CORE metas cover all 457,200 outcomes, median 8.5; llama32-11 is the outlier at 32.9.
addenda_notes.FGOBJ_CALIBRATION: 2,400 clean forwards per COCO block (6 fine-grained questions x 400 calibration rows); the table follows the campaign convention (COCO x 22 models). It is 3/8 of the COCO CALIBRATION module, i.e. 0.02-0.14 GPU-h per block on the measured CALIBRATION throughput, under 2% of the FGOBJ block it accompanies.

semend.purpose: semantic endpoints outside the six yes/no / A-B templates, so ownership is not validated only against the model's own answers under those six prompts

templates.NY: Is there no evidence of {finding} in {image_phrase}? Answer yes or no.
templates.DA: Which is present in {image_phrase}, {finding} or {competitor}? Answer A if it is {finding} and B if it is {competitor}. Reply with A or B only.
templates.DB: Which is present in {image_phrase}, {competitor} or {finding}? Answer A if it is {competitor} and B if it is {finding}. Reply with A or B only.

endpoint.NY: negated question; the endpoint is p(yes) with SIGN -1, because a direction that carries the concept must move a negated question the other way
endpoint.DA: two-finding forced choice with the concept as option A; the endpoint is the probability of the CONCEPT option
endpoint.DB: the same forced choice with the order and the A/B mapping swapped (counterbalanced); the endpoint is again the probability of the concept option
endpoint.RF: short report continuation; the endpoint is log p(finding word) = max(positive_logits) - vocab_logsumexp at the continuation position, no yes/no head

candidate_source.RF: first token of each spelling of the finding word (positive) and of the dataset's neutral word (negative)

semend.competitor: the question's strongest competitor in the block's own CORE write matrix, argmax_{d != q} W_qd on the primary template; frozen by the prep into fits/vis.last/semend_seed0.npz

report_prefix.nih: Write the findings section of the radiology report for this chest radiograph.
report_prefix.chexpert: Write the findings section of the radiology report for this chest radiograph.
report_prefix.coco: List the objects visible in this photograph.

semend.grid: per (question, endpoint): clean baseline + the SIX label directions + the SIX answer directions a_d + the question's label sham + the question's answer sham + 18 random directions = 33 conditions, of which 32 are steered and therefore fill exactly one batch-32 forward; the endpoint grid costs the same GPU time as a grid half its size would
semend.reference: per endpoint and per family, the own signed effect must be positive, above every one of the 18 random directions (rank 1 of 19) and above the |effect| of that family's own sham

attrq.purpose: cheap per-block eligibility pass for the ATTR / ATTRRAND control: how well the model answers each non-clinical attribute question under three phrasings, on the calibration rows, with no writes and no reference family. It exists because a cell whose clean answer no direction can move cannot be owned for reasons that have nothing to do with whether the concept is clinical, so pooling such cells makes the attribute-versus-finding comparison unfair in both directions.

AQ1.text: Was {image_phrase} acquired with an anteroposterior (AP) projection? Answer yes or no.

AQ2.text: Does {image_phrase} show an AP (anteroposterior) view rather than a PA (posteroanterior) view? Answer yes or no.

AQ1.text: Is the patient in {image_phrase} female? Answer yes or no.

AQ2.text: Does {image_phrase} show a female patient rather than a male patient? Answer yes or no.

AQ1.text: Is the patient in {image_phrase} sixty years old or older? Answer yes or no.

AQ2.text: Does {image_phrase} show a patient aged sixty or older rather than a younger patient? Answer yes or no.

attrq.answer_mapping: yes = the attribute is positive (view_AP = AP / portable, sex_F = female, age_60 = age >= 60), exactly the mapping the yes/no templates use for a finding; AQ1 and AQ2 keep the 'Answer yes or no.' ending and reuse the block's frozen IY candidate set, so nothing about the answer head changes.
attrq.AQ0: the phrasing ATTR and ATTRRAND already write: the block's primary template with the attribute phrase in the {finding} slot, rendered by protocol.render_question, so its text is byte-identical to theirs and the module measures the written question as well as the alternatives.
attrq.eligibility_source: AQ0 inherits the primary template's preflight eligibility; AQ1 and AQ2 are yes/no questions and inherit IY's, so a block whose yes/no mapping failed image-free preflight check E does not score them.
attrq.selection_rule: per block and attribute the primary phrasing is the ELIGIBLE phrasing with the highest one-sided 95% lower bound of the clean-answer AUROC against the attribute's manifest label on the calibration rows. Eligible = >= 10 known positives and >= 10 known negatives, >= 1900 valid unit-bootstrap draws and a lower bound above 0.5 -- the support and lower-bound rule the readable and answer-capable grades use. Ties break in phrasing order (AQ0 first). An attribute with no eligible phrasing is recorded as not answerable in that block and no phrasing is selected.
attrq.bootstrap: cftransfer.analysis.bootstrap_indices(dataset, n_calibration, BOOT_CALIBRATION_SEED, draws), the campaign's shared calibration-row unit bootstrap
attrq.writes: none: alpha 0 clean forwards only, one condition per (row, attribute, phrasing)
attrq.analysis: cftransfer.analysis --what attrq: per attribute and phrasing the question text, n_pos / n_neg, clean-answer AUROC and Brier, the one-sided 95% lower bound, the answer-capable flag, and the selected phrasing with the reason; written to summary.json under `attrq`. analysis --what attr then reads the written phrasing's calibration-row numbers from it, so an attribute cell and a clinical cell carry answerability measured on the same rows.

attr_comparison.purpose: the attribute-versus-finding ownership comparison of the ATTR / ATTRRAND control, reported three ways. All three are prespecified and all three are reported whatever they show.

modes.all_cells: every attribute cell against every clinical cell of the same blocks (the comparison as it stood)
modes.answer_capable_cells: only cells whose clean answer clears the campaign's answer-capable rule (>= 10 known positives and negatives, >= 1900 valid draws, one-sided 95% lower AUROC bound above 0.5), applied to attributes and findings alike
modes.answerability_matched: each attribute cell paired with every clinical cell of the SAME block whose clean-answer AUROC is within match_window of it; the reported quantity is the ownership rate of each kind over the matched pairs and their difference. Attribute cells with no match are counted and named.

answer_auroc_source.clinical: summary.json `calibration` of the same block: the clean CALIBRATION margins of the primary template against the manifest label on the 400 calibration rows. Read, never recomputed.
answer_auroc_source.attribute: summary.json `attrq` for the phrasing ATTR wrote, when ATTRQ has been scored for the block (400 calibration rows, same rows as the clinical number); otherwise summary.json `attr`, which measures the ATTR module's own clean baseline against the manifest attribute label on the 600 test rows. Every cell records which one it used.
answer_auroc_source.caveat: until ATTRQ is scored the two kinds are measured on different rows (600 test vs 400 calibration) and therefore with different bootstrap power at the same AUROC, which makes the answer-capable flag easier to reach for an attribute cell than for a clinical one. ATTRQ removes the asymmetry; the aggregates report the row set and the known-label counts of both kinds so it stays visible.

attr_comparison.ownership: cftransfer.manifest.owned: steering_reference and verdict == fixed_family_advantage, unchanged
attr_comparison.interval: percentile 2.5 / 97.5 over the campaign's shared unit (patient) bootstrap draws of the block analysis (core_bootstrap_indices, seed 2026090601): ownership is re-decided inside every draw as steering_reference (the point-estimate reference) and O_q > 0 with the strongest competitor recomputed in that draw, because the max-T simultaneous verdict is not a per-draw quantity. The point rates use the campaign's owned() rule; the per-draw rate is reported beside them so the gap between the two rules is visible.
attr_comparison.report: <RUN_ROOT>/robustness/round2.json attr.comparison, per dataset and pooled over the chest sets, with the per-block rows carrying every cell's answer AUROC, its source and its matched partners
